description:
Found during the fz-kdt.13 build, latent at HEAD. World::demand_producer_if_needed
(drive.rs:~251) checks the rebased flag BEFORE the blocked check. The rebase
flag is only cleared by a CONCLUDING run, so a job that repeatedly blocks
stays flagged forever and every stall pass re-enqueues it -- re-running it
straight back into the same unsatisfied waits.

Latent today: with no scheduler Settled-waiters, the re-runs happen to be
harmless (measured: fixing the order changes nothing at HEAD -- 969/1667/2864
evaluations byte-identical on the three target fixtures). The moment settled
waits exist on the agenda path it produces UNCAUSED evaluations (measured
live during the kdt.13 experiment: 51/5/49 uncaused across the fixtures,
e.g. Enum.reduce/3 analysis: 24 evaluations, 16 uncaused, 20 blocked).

Fix: check blocked first. Sound because Scheduler::enqueue_dependents never
marks a job rebased without enqueueing it in the same step, so shifted ground
has already been offered to the job. TDD: scheduler/world-level red test --
a repeatedly-blocking rebased job must not be re-enqueued by the stall pass
while its waits are unsatisfied.
title: demand_producer_if_needed re-enqueues blocked jobs forever: blocked must gate before rebased
